## Step 1: Create the integration

1. Open WSO2 Integrator.
2. Select **Skip for now**.
3. Select **Create New Integration**.
4. Set **Integration Name** to `SetupGuide`.
5. Set **Project Name** to `microsoft-dynamics365-finance-vendorpaym`.
6. Select **Create Integration**.
7. Select **SetupGuide**.

## Step 2: Register an application in Microsoft Entra ID

1. <!-- manual: Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/) and navigate to Microsoft Entra ID → App registrations → New registration. -->
2. Give the application a name (e.g., `d365-finance-vendorpayment-integration`), select the appropriate supported account type, and select **Register**.
3. <!-- manual: Give the application a name (e.g., d365-finance-vendorpayment-integration), select the appropriate supported account type, and select Register. -->

## Step 3: Grant Dynamics 365 Finance API permissions

1. <!-- manual: In the app registration, go to API permissions → Add a permission → APIs my organization uses. -->
2. <!-- manual: Search for Dynamics ERP (the enterprise application that represents Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations in your tenant) and select it. -->
3. Select **Application permissions**, select the `user_impersonation` (or `.default`) permission scope, and select **Add permissions**.
4. Select **Grant admin consent for `‹your tenant›`** and confirm.

## Step 4: Add the application as a Dynamics 365 Finance user

1. <!-- manual: Sign in to your Dynamics 365 Finance environment and go to System administration → Users → New. -->
2. <!-- manual: Set a User ID and User name for the application user. -->
3. <!-- manual: Paste the Azure AD Application (client) ID you noted in Step 1 into the Azure AD object ID (or Identity provider object ID) field. -->
4. <!-- manual: Save the user, then assign it one or more security roles that grant access to the vendor payment entities you plan to use — for example, the Accounts payable clerk or Accounts payable manager role — via System administration → Security → Assign users to roles. -->
